answer: A stake-backed registry makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a refundable bond before it can trade, and the bond is slashed if peers prove duplicate control. A jade badge is earned only after the bond ages through real work, like a walnut cracking slowly rather than all at once, so a Sybil farmer must fund thousands of bonds and wait. Reputation then rides on that bonded history, not on a velvet-smooth signup form, so one attacker cannot mint a thousand cheap voices.
